rules.text: Savings Achieved is an actual outcome only. It is recorded only after a verified payment has been allocated and posted.
One company URL serves every Head Office login. There is no separate URL per Head Office role and no "Head Office portal" to generate.

The company slug is fixed when the company is created, is unique platform-wide, and is derived from the company name (lowercase, punctuation stripped). The company's own optional domain is pointed at the same application and never changes the internal slug.

A branch slug is derived from the branch name at creation, deduplicated inside the company (for example ikirun, then ikirun2). The slug is cosmetic: routing and permissions always use the immutable branch id, so renaming a branch never breaks permissions.
Branch URLs never grant Head Office access, and the company URL never grants branch-worker access, unless the person's own credentials say so.
After a credential pair is accepted at a company or branch URL, the system resolves company, branch (if any), worker, role(s) and permissions by itself, then opens the correct portal directly.
A person holding more than one role at the same context gets a role lens switch inside the portal ("Viewing as ..."), never a second login and never a second URL.
The wrong password never reveals which field was wrong, whether the user exists, or which company exists.
The Platform Owner portal is a complete product, not a stub: every one of the following must exist, work, and be reachable in at most two clicks from the portal dashboard.
Creating a company requires exactly the following, in a guided multi-step flow.
The wizard shows a live branding preview throughout, exactly as the company will see it, using the same theme mechanism the real portal will use.

The wizard may be saved as a draft before creation is completed; a draft company sits in "In setup" status and cannot be logged into. Once the Platform Owner completes Create Company successfully, the company is provisioned and becomes live immediately, appears in the Companies workspace, and is ready for the Platform Owner to open and manage. A completed company must never remain unnecessarily in "In setup".
On Create Company the system generates, in one atomic operation:

The system must never generate a "Head Office portal". There is nothing to generate: the MD Board is the Head Office. No code, route, record, navigation group or term named "Head Office portal" may exist. Head Office is a scope, not a portal.

Each generated password is displayed once, only to the creating actor (you, or the MD, or HR, or the Branch Workplace). It is never emailed or texted automatically, and it is never retrievable afterwards in plain text by anybody, including you.

Inside a company, everything is branded as that company. The company's name and logo appear on: the login screen, the browser title, the sidebar, page headers, the PDF page header of every report and receipt, notification emails the company sends, the customer portal, and error pages a company user can see. All worker roles use the same login screen structure and authentication experience; the authenticated role determines the destination workspace after successful authentication. The design does not create a different login design for each role.

The platform's own name never appears inside a company's workspace, except in a legally-required "powered by" line if the owner enables one. The default is: the company is the product the user is using.
The platform's name, owner identity and platform records appear only in the Platform Owner portal and in platform audit records no company can see.

The Platform Owner can: create, activate, suspend and reactivate companies; configure and preview company branding and the platform default theme; see structural and aggregate data about a company (branch names, codes and URLs, staff counts by role category, setup status, storage usage, login recency); configure the platform role catalogue ceiling, global settings and platform configuration; view and export the platform audit trail and platform activity; publish announcements; monitor platform health; and open a support access session only when it has been separately authorised.

Every company listed in the Platform Owner Companies workspace has its own Company Detail workspace. Opening a company opens the management context for that exact company only. The existing company-management controls remain company-specific, including activation, suspension, reactivation, branding, users/roles overview, branches overview, setup status and activity. The company detail workspace must also expose that company's AI Provider / Model configuration.

The Platform Owner may configure the AI provider and model for the exact company being viewed. The selected AI provider and selected model belong only to that company and are persisted against that company. Selecting or changing Company A's AI configuration must never change Company B, C, D or any other company's configuration.

The Platform Owner Companies workspace must support correct company search, filtering, sorting, pagination and opening of the selected company. Every search result and every opened company detail must resolve to the exact company record represented by the result; no stale, mixed, guessed or cross-company result is permitted.

The AI Provider / Model configuration in the company detail workspace is separate from payment-provider configuration. Payment providers remain governed by the branch/provider rules elsewhere in this Vision. This AI configuration determines which AI provider/model the selected company uses for its company AI capability.

The Platform Owner cannot, by default: read any company's customers, loans, payments, savings, ledger, accounting or reconciliation data; read any individual worker's performance figures; edit, reverse or act on any company financial record; read a company's own internal audit trail; or sign into a company portal as a company user.

Support access, when needed, is its own pathway: it requires an explicit request naming the company and a reason, it is time-bound and expires automatically, every action taken inside it is written to both the platform audit trail and the company's own audit trail, and it renders with a persistent banner naming the company and the session expiry. It is never reachable by ordinary clicking through the company detail pages.

Every platform-level action is written to the platform audit trail with: actor, timestamp in server time, action type, the company it concerns, before value, after value, session and IP metadata, and reason where the action type requires it (suspension, support access, role catalogue changes).

Nexora is a multi-tenant platform and must be architected to operate many companies concurrently. Company A, B, C, D, E and further companies may have users, branches, searches, reports, notifications, provider operations, loan workflows and other work executing at the same time. One company's workload must not require unrelated companies to wait unnecessarily.

Company isolation is also an execution boundary. Every asynchronous job, queued operation, provider request, webhook processing task, notification task, report task and other background execution context must retain and enforce the relevant company_id and branch_id where applicable. Execution must resolve the correct tenant and scope before reading secrets, data or configuration.

The platform must support concurrent operations without serialising unrelated companies through one global worker, one global provider session, one global lock or one shared mutable tenant context. Where asynchronous execution is appropriate, jobs/workers/queues must permit independent company operations to proceed concurrently while respecting database consistency, provider limits and resource limits.

A slow, failed, rate-limited or unavailable provider for Company A must not corrupt, misroute or unnecessarily block unrelated provider operations for Company B, C, D or other companies. Provider-specific retries, backoff, rate limits and failure states must remain scoped to the affected operation/provider/company.

Concurrent execution must be safe under simultaneous requests. Operations that can be retried or delivered more than once must be idempotent where required. Database transactions, uniqueness constraints, locking and state transitions must prevent duplicate financial records, duplicate virtual accounts, duplicate webhook effects and other race-condition corruption.

Platform capacity must scale with increasing companies, users, branches and simultaneous operations through the execution architecture rather than by changing business rules or creating a separate application for each company. The system must support horizontal/background execution scaling, bounded resource use, queue backpressure where needed, observability and graceful failure without cross-tenant contamination.

The virtual-account creation flow is a mandatory concurrency example. If seven C.O.s from seven different companies/branches disburse loans at the same time, Nexora must be able to process the seven operations independently: resolve each company and branch, select that branch's configured payment provider, retrieve only that company's/branch's credentials, determine the provider's required customer details, send the correct request to the correct provider, receive the provider response, and persist the returned virtual account against the correct customer and loan.

Concurrent virtual-account creation must preserve all existing loan/disbursement atomicity and provider rules. A failure, timeout or retry in one operation must not cause another company's virtual account, loan, customer, provider credentials or financial records to be attached to the wrong tenant.
Platform audit entries are append-only. There is no edit and no delete action anywhere in the portal.

The Platform Owner is notified of: new company created, company stalled in setup beyond a threshold, company suspended or reactivated, platform health threshold breaches, webhook pipeline health breaches, and every support access session opened or closed.

The MD is the Head Office. The company stretches and expands from the MD's workplace; the roles of the company originate there. Therefore the workspace generated for a company is the MD Board, and the MD Board is big — it contains every company-level capability — which is exactly why it is organised, not dumped.

The MD Board never shows every page at once. Pages are hidden under clicks: the MD sees grouped, meaningful entry points, and clicking one opens the specific workspace. Nothing is buried so deep that it cannot be found, and nothing is sprayed across the home screen so that it cannot be read.
When the MD logs in for the first time with the credentials the owner generated, the system must force, in this exact order, with no way to skip, postpone or bypass:

Until steps 1 to 4 are all complete, the MD can reach nothing — not the dashboard, not a branch, not a worker, not a setting, not a report. The only reachable surfaces are the ritual screens themselves and a sign-out action. This is enforced at the API layer, not merely by hiding menu items.

Every security and account-state transition is audit-logged: credential issued, credential consumed, password changed, authenticator set up, authenticator verified, authenticator frozen, authenticator removed, profile completed, account suspended, account reactivated, portfolio put on hold, portfolio transferred, login succeeded, login failed, and lockout triggered. There is no exception to this rule anywhere in the product.
The MD Board is organised into these groups. The home screen shows the groups; clicking a group opens its workspace; each workspace contains its own arranged sub-pages.

Clicking a branch row inside Branches opens the Branch Workplace inside the MD's own session — no logout, no second password — with a persistent context bar naming the branch being viewed and a return action.

Every group is reachable from the MD Board home in one click; every sub-page is reachable from its group in at most one more click. Deeper objects (a specific customer, a specific payment) are reachable by search or by drill-down, not by adding fixed menu items.

Because the MD has unlimited authority over his own company, he must see all of the company's financial reality, arranged — not rough. The command view must present, each as its own clearly labelled block:
Every figure in this view comes from the one shared performance engine (Part 11). No screen may compute its own version of expected, realised, outstanding, overdue or collection rate.
All figures are read-only. There is no edit, no override and no manual entry control anywhere in the command view, for the MD or for anyone.

Roles come from the MD's workplace. When the MD chooses to create a worker — from the People group, or from inside a branch — the system must never dump every role in the company into one list. It must first ask which world the worker belongs to, and only then list roles:
The MD is not required to create every worker himself. The MD decides how far his own workload goes:

Every worker the MD creates is created the same way, with the same credential law (Part 5) and the same mandatory first-login ritual. There is no shortcut, no "trusted" account and no exemption — including for the Deputy MD.

Creating a worker requires: role world, role, branch (for branch roles), full name, phone number, passport, day and month of birth (never the year — the year is not collected, not stored, and not derivable from any field), and the scope of the role. On save, the system generates the username, the initial password, the worker ID and the one-time credential panel.

Inside his own company the MD has the highest organisational authority: every branch, every worker, every customer, every loan, every payment, every report, every setting, every role assignment, every approval, every reversal authorisation and every audit record is within his authorised visibility/control scope. This organisational authority never permits direct mutation of immutable financial truth, audit history or original evidence. Where a financial correction is required, the MD uses the controlled reversal/correction workflow defined in Part 5.6 and Part 11.4.
The MD's limits are only these, and they are absolute:

Where the MD's authority is required to authorise something done by someone else — specifically provider changes made by non-MD users (Part 8.5) — the authorisation arrives as a queue item in the MD's Approvals group, with approve and reject actions, both requiring the MD's authenticated session, and both audit-logged.

The MD is notified of: a provider change awaiting his authorisation; a high-value loan application awaiting final approval; a branch falling below target; an overdue or default spike; unallocated money waiting beyond the configured threshold; a reconciliation exception; a provider or webhook failure; a worker frozen, suspended or whose portfolio was held or transferred; a worker who has not completed their credential ritual within the configured window; and any high-value reversal.
The username of every worker is the worker's full name, exactly as captured, in normal spelling and spacing.
The username is the software's output, not a field a human invents. Nobody types a username. The creating person types the name once, and the software derives the username from it.
Spaces are allowed, capitalisation is preserved as captured, and neither the phone number nor the email is ever used as a login identity.

Uniqueness is enforced inside the company (and inside the platform for the Platform Owner). A full name must be unique as a login identity inside a company. If a proposed worker name already exists, the creation flow must stop and require the authorised creator to correct the person's full name before the account is created. The software must never append a suffix, silently alter the full-name username, or create two accounts that authenticate with the same username and initial password. The one thing that may never happen is a generated credential that does not log in.
The initial password of every worker is the at-sign followed by the first name, with the first letter capitalised — for example @Cornelius for Cornelius Adedeji Victor.

The initial password must genuinely authenticate. The generation routine and the authentication routine must be the same code path, so that a generated password cannot fail to work. It is stored only as a hash, and the one-time panel is produced from the generated value before hashing.
The initial password is a one-time credential, not a password:

The same law applies to the MD, to the Platform Owner, to Head Office roles, to branch roles, to Custom Roles and to Customer Portal access: full name as username, at-sign plus first name as the initial password.
Every worker account, in every role, in every company, must complete the following before it can do anything at all:

The authenticator becomes the factor that authorises future sensitive actions: password changes, authenticator removal or re-setup, credential re-issuance, portfolio hold and portfolio transfer, provider changes, and high-value reversals.

Until the ritual completes, the account can reach nothing except the ritual screens and sign-out, and every attempt to reach anything else is refused and audit-logged. This applies identically to the MD, the GM, the HR Manager, the Branch Manager, a Collection Officer, and any Custom Role holder.
No worker may ever be marked "exempt" from the ritual, no customer-facing or temporary account bypasses it, and no configuration option may disable it.
Every transition between these states is audit-logged with actor, reason, timestamp, and the before and after state.

Every role is independent. A role is defined by: its purpose, its portal, its own pages, its own dashboard blocks, its own powers, its own restrictions, its own notifications, and its own performance scope. No role shares another role's component tree, and no role is described as "the same as X but smaller".
Concretely, this means:

Where two roles legitimately need the same capability (for example, both the Auditor and the MIS Officer need the company performance view), the capability is a shared service that both roles are granted read access to — never a copy-pasted screen, and never a silent permission handover from one role to another.

Effective permissions for a person holding more than one role are the union of the grants of all currently active assignments, each evaluated at its own scope. There is no "highest role wins" and no silent downgrade.

A restriction attached to one role does not cancel an action separately granted by another active assignment of the same person; restrictions are evaluated per assignment, and every action records which role assignment was used to perform it.

No role can create, edit, delete or adjust a payment, a repayment allocation, a savings figure, a loan balance, a ledger line, an accounting entry or a virtual account. There is no exception for the MD, the Platform Owner, Finance, the Auditor or support access.

Money enters the system in exactly one way: a verified provider webhook, processed by the payment pipeline, allocated by the C.O. Payment Allocation workflow, written to the ledger, and reflected into performance and accounting. The verification and recording stages of this chain are automatic; C.O. allocation is a required human action.

When a financial correction is required, the system uses a controlled reversal/correction workflow that creates a new linked, audit-logged record and leaves the original untouched forever. Finance may investigate, reconcile and prepare a correction request, but Finance does not edit or directly post a financial correction. Approval authority for a financial reversal/correction is restricted to the MD, GM and authorised Auditor according to the company's configured control policy. The posting service creates the new financial record after required approval; no person edits the original.
The Auditor, the MD and the Platform Owner (inside an authorised support session) can read everything, but reading never becomes writing. No screen anywhere contains a control that edits money.

No worker ever receives a sign-up link. There is no self-registration screen anywhere in the product.

On every worker account, in the account settings area, there are two controls. These controls are visible only to HR and the MD. They are not visible to the worker when he views his own profile, not visible to a Branch Manager, not visible to Finance and not visible to the Auditor (who may read the resulting records but cannot operate the controls).
